answer: Each seat binds to one never-seated DNSSEC-signed domain and a 150 POA lock. Mid-epoch, three resolvers — over a canyon rim, from a harbor inlet cache, and from a recursive on a desert dune — query TXT at _poa.<domain> for H(epoch-seed || domain) and require a CT-logged certificate covering that name within 90 seconds. A second key on the same eTLD+1, or a CNAME already seating another agent, burns 75 POA and merges both claims. Names stay locked four epochs so cheap label rotation buys no extra weight; leftover collateral refunds after three sealed answers; CT logs stay public for replay.
